outcome: Vascular flow within the inner half of the myometrium
Pain score (during menstruation and transvaginal examination)
Presence of adhesions (inferred from reduced mobility)
cohort: A total of 92 women, comprising 46 with a history of menorrhagia and 46 healthy controls, participated in the study.
finding: Women with menorrhagia exhibited significantly larger uterine volume, reduced uterine mobility, higher rates of vascular flow within the inner half of the myometrium, and higher pain scores compared to controls.
